root_causes.description: The frontend container was terminated ('Killing: Stopping container frontend') and replaced by a freshly scheduled pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8, causing a collapse of frontend server request rate (p50 dropped to ~8 from a mean of ~148). No downstream service shows elevated errors, so the disruption originates at the frontend pod itself, consistent with a container crash/restart.

evidence.expected_baseline: no container-kill events for frontend during steady state

evidence.query_or_id: Scheduled: Successfully assigned otel-demo/frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 to otel-sre-copilot-control-plane (count=1)
evidence.expected_baseline: no new frontend pod creation during steady state
steady frontend server request rate ~148/s with no collapse

root_causes.description: Frontend server p99 latency is elevated (~6.1 s p50 of the quantile series, up to 7.9 s) during the window, which could reflect requests stalled while the pod was being killed/replaced; however no latency anomaly flag was raised and error rate stayed flat, making this a secondary/derived symptom rather than the primary fault.

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p99 latency in low hundreds of ms during steady state

root_causes.description: A downstream dependency failure was considered because frontend calls checkout, cart, recommendation, product-catalog, shipping, currency and ad; however error_rate for checkout (0.004), product-catalog (0.000) and recommendation (0.000) all remained at baseline, so a downstream-triggered failure is not supported.

remediation_steps: Confirm frontend pod restart/crash: kubectl -n otel-demo get pods -l app=frontend and kubectl describe pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 (inspect Last State, Reason, Exit Code).
Inspect the terminated frontend container's previous logs (kubectl logs <prior-frontend-pod> --previous) to distinguish OOMKill, liveness-probe kill, or application crash.
Review frontend resource requests/limits and liveness/readiness probe thresholds; increase memory limit or relax probe timeouts if a kill was probe- or OOM-driven.
Verify downstream calls (checkout, cart, recommendation, product-catalog) remained healthy and add pod-restart alerting on frontend to catch recurrence early.
